newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end two pct down but above day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end two pct down but above day's lows.

text.p: Italian stocks fell on Monday ending the day almost two percent lower, although losses were smaller than feared due to a calming start on Wall Street.
U.S. stocks began slightly up in New York after suffering their worst drop in percentage terms on Friday since November 1991.
Italian investors who dreaded another sell-off on Wall Street on Monday breathed a collective sigh of relief.
"We expected to see some declines today, since our market was shut for a holiday on Friday," said a Milan trader.

Italy's all-share Mibtel Index fell 280 points, or 1.94 percent, to 14,125, and the blue-chip Mib 30 was down 2.1 percent at 21,290. Leading shares were mainly lower, with banking shares the hardest hit.
With most of Italy's stores, factories and corporate headquarters shuttered for the month-long summer holiday, traders looked to the U.S. market for direction.
Concern that the U.S. and German central banks could raise interest rates this week is making some investors cautious, but analysts do not expect action from either bank.
The U.S. policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday, and the Bundesbank monetary council meets Thursday.
Traders said about 1.1 trillion lire ($617 million) in shares changed hands, which is above-average volume during the month of August.

Most-active shares were state-controlled energy company Eni, telephone monopoly Telecom Italia, agro-chemicals conglomerate Montedison, and cellular phone company Telecom Italia Mobile, which fell 3.98 percent to 5,783.
Alitalia, the loss-making state-held airline, was the biggest loser of the day as it fell 5.4 percent.

Banca Commerciale Italiana shares fell 3.5 percent as investors decided to take profits from previous gains, while among smaller capitalised companies, luxury jewellery maker Bulgari fell 4.6 percent to 10,210.
Among gainers, financial holding Gemina rose 2.8 percent to 599 while Banco Ambrosiano Veneto rose 0.4 percent to 9,800.
